item.content:encoded:
Metaplanet cut its 2026 revenue forecast by 59% on November 13, to ¥6.5 billion from ¥16 billion. Its operating profit forecast fell 74%, to ¥3 billion from ¥11.4 billion.

The Tokyo-listed Bitcoin (BTC) treasury firm traced the cut to its own discounted stock. Metaplanet stock fell 4.37% to ¥219 that day, down 53.21% so far in 2026.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Why a Cheap Stock Starved the Bitcoin Machine

The original target assumed Metaplanet could keep raising money at its late-2025 pace. That cash was meant to buy more Bitcoin and grow its options-based Bitcoin Income business.

The plan stalled once mNAV stayed below 1x. That ratio compares the company’s market value with its Bitcoin. At that level, new shares would dilute the Bitcoin held per share. So Metaplanet held back on share sales. Bitcoin purchases and income business volume both came in below plan.

The ¥52 billion convertible bond issued in October will not fill the gap.

Metaplanet will put those proceeds toward share buybacks first. That leaves limited funds for new Bitcoin or the income business, according to the filing.

Costs also climb in the fourth quarter. Metaplanet will consolidate Metaplanet Securities and book goodwill amortization from that acquisition.

What the Numbers Say About the Final Quarter

The revised targets look harsher next to results so far this year. Nine-month revenue rose 30.5% to ¥5.9 billion, per Metaplanet’s results. Operating profit grew 26.5% to about ¥3.5 billion.

Yet losses on Bitcoin valuation and a third-quarter Bitcoin sale left a ¥27.2 billion net loss.

The new forecast implies only about ¥600 million in fourth-quarter revenue. Revenue averaged nearly ¥2 billion per quarter through September.

Operating profit already exceeds the ¥3 billion full-year goal, which points to a fourth-quarter operating loss.

The ¥6.5 billion target also sits 27% below 2025 revenue of ¥8.9 billion. The original target, set on February 16, implied about 80% growth.

Is the Bitcoin Treasury Playbook Running Dry?

Metaplanet says its Bitcoin-centered strategy remains unchanged. Still, the growth model relied on selling stock priced above the Bitcoin behind it.

With mNAV below 1x, that funding route has narrowed, and buybacks now take priority.

More pressure comes on November 30. That day, MSCI drops Metaplanet from its Japan Small Cap Index and Strategy from its USA Index.

Its new removal rules target companies that behave like investment vehicles. Funds tracking those benchmarks will need to sell the shares.

More pressure comes on November 30. That day, MSCI removes Metaplanet and Strategy from its indexes, following its index removal rules for Bitcoin treasuries. Funds tracking those benchmarks will need to sell their holdings.

A sustained mNAV recovery above 1x would reopen equity funding and weaken this read.

However, other traders see a bottom forming soon. Is Bitcoin’s Record High Gone for Good? Bitcoin’s slide from its $126,080 peak has fueled intense

The post Will Bitcoin Never Set Another All-Time High? Analysts Debate On X appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin price fell below $68,000 on November 13. The price now sits more than 45% below its record high of $126,080.

Some analysts are saying that the peak will never return. However, other traders see a bottom forming soon.

Is Bitcoin’s Record High Gone for Good?

Bitcoin’s slide from its $126,080 peak has fueled intense debate. Some traders view it as a healthy pullback within a bull market. Others fear a more permanent shift.

Analyst Z believes Bitcoin will never revisit it.

“Mark my words. You will never see another Bitcoin all-time high in your lifetime,” he wrote in a widely shared post on X.

According to the analyst, the investment environment has changed:

  • Higher interest rates discourage leveraged speculation.
  • Meanwhile, AI companies and new listings such as SpaceX now compete for capital.

Moreover, he described a reported $6.3 billion Binance-related incident as the symbolic end of an era.

Those claims remain highly contested. Still, the post quickly drew wide attention among crypto traders.

“Type of tweets you see at the bottom. I’ve also never seen a good take starting with ‘mark my words’. See you at the next ATH,” The Crypto Monk replied.

Could Bitcoin Be Near a Bottom Instead?

Not everyone agrees. Michaël van de Poppe acknowledged the severity of the correction. Still, he suggested that a bottom could form within a day or two.

“…I’m keen to see how this day’s candle closes. If #Bitcoin repeats the same price action as prior to the SpaceX IPO, the bottom should be hit today/tomorrow and we’ll only go up from here,” van de Poppe said.

Similarly, Merlijn The Trader sees a possible repeat of the 2023 structure. He plans to bid near $68,000, with a weekly close below $60,000 as his invalidation level.

However, Ted Pillows noted that open interest remains elevated. In his view, the market still needs a leverage flush before a lasting reversal.

On-chain data adds some optimism. According to CryptoQuant’s analyst MAC_D, the latest drawdown of roughly 19% exceeds the 14.39% average bull-market correction. Short-term holder SOPR has also reached levels that marked major bottoms in past cycles.

For now, the 200-week moving average near $67,975 acts as immediate support. A break below could open the $66,000 to $67,000 zone, followed by $62,300.

On the upside, reclaiming $75,000 would signal renewed strength. Meanwhile, a weekly close below $60,000 would send a clear warning to the bulls.

The post Will Bitcoin Never Set Another All-Time High? Analysts Debate On X appeared first on BeInCrypto.

The post Crypto Market’s Nearly 6% Slide Costs Bulls $1 Billion in a Day appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Crypto traders lost $1.23 billion to forced liquidations over the past 24 hours, nearly double the previous day’s total. Bets on higher prices accounted for $1.02 billion of it as the crypto market cap fell 5.75% to $2.33 trillion.

Long positions made up 82.7% of the crypto liquidations, Coinglass data shows. Bitcoin (BTC) slipped below $68,000 to test its 200-week average. A weekly close below that line on Sunday could expose holders to a deeper retest.

Bitcoin Longs Lose Twice as Much as a Day Earlier

Bitcoin positions accounted for $637.24 million of the total, with longs at 90.8%. That is nearly double the $325.28 million in Bitcoin liquidations BeInCrypto reported a day earlier.

Ethereum (ETH) followed at $256.52 million, where 76.3% came from long bets.

In all, 163,631 traders were liquidated, up from 112,947 the day before. The largest single order was a $17.81 million Ethereum short on Binance, closed at $1,979.21.

About $1 billion of the total hit in the first 12 hours of the window. Liquidations have eased since, with $233.07 million over the past 12 hours and $41.01 million over the past four.

The liquidations hit as a broader sell-off spread across crypto markets.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Can Bitcoin Hold Its 200-Week Average?

Bitcoin traded at $67,623, per BeInCrypto Markets data. It fell 3.70% over 24 hours. The cryptocurrency is now testing its 200-week simple moving average (SMA) near $67,922, trading just below it. 

BeInCrypto’s analysis of the sell-off noted that the same average caught Bitcoin in July and launched its August rally.

The first floor under the average sits between $66,000 and $67,000. That range blocked Bitcoin’s recoveries from June through August.

Should that range fail, the next level is $62,300. Buyers defended that price twice this year, in late February and again before the late-August breakout. The last time Bitcoin slipped beneath it, in July, the drop bottomed near $58,000.

On the upside, $75,000 is the first hurdle if Bitcoin rebounds.

Has Ethereum Lost the Base of Its August Breakout?

Ethereum’s price fell 3.37% to $1,903.78, per BeInCrypto Markets data.

It now trades below $1,920.51, a Fibonacci support level flagged by analyst More Crypto Online. The analyst’s next support sits at $1,832.78.

Beyond Sunday’s weekly close, two dates could set the next direction for both majors. MSCI drops Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its benchmark indexes on November 30.

The Federal Reserve then announces its rate decision on December 9. Long bets have absorbed most of the liquidations for two straight days, so bullish traders carry the most exposure into both events

item.title: Can Elon Musk Bring Jensen Huang Back as Nvidia CEO?
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Elon Musk backs a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang, but only Nvidia's board can make him CEO again. Here's what it takes.

The post Can Elon Musk Bring Jensen Huang Back as Nvidia CEO? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk wants Jensen Huang back in charge of Nvidia. The company’s internal rules give Musk no vote.

Huang resigned as CEO on November 12 while the board investigated his ties to a woman US officials link to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia shares closed that day 11% below their November 6 level.

Could Jensen Huang Come Back TO Nvidia?

Nvidia’s board would have to vote him back. Under the company’s bylaws, a majority of directors in office controls who holds executive posts.

After Huang’s resignation from Nvidia, that means six of the 10 remaining directors. Shareholders get no direct vote on the CEO.

Huang’s own shares cannot force a return. He controls about 3.58% of the votes, according to Nvidia’s 2026 proxy. BlackRock and Vanguard each hold more than 7%.

Musk has no seat on that board. Still, he publicly backed a comeback on Friday.

“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too,” said Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX.

The nearest precedent is OpenAI in 2023. Its board rehired Sam Altman within days after about 97% of staff threatened to quit.

However, OpenAI was a private company. Most of the directors who removed Altman also left its board.

Inside Nvidia, an internal post urging Huang’s return drew more than 1,600 comments.

The Foreign Intelligence Probe Matters More Than Musk’s Petition

The board’s own investigation stands in the way. On November 8, directors began examining whether a foreign spy operation had targeted Huang.

They later hired law firm Wachtell Lipton, led by former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim. Bloomberg reported that directors left Huang no option but to resign.

Washington is also involved. The House Foreign Affairs Committee wants Huang to appear on December 1 and has warned of a subpoena.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren said his exit does not clear him of responsibility. President Donald Trump, by contrast, has praised Huang publicly.

For shareholders, the outcome carries a price tag. Analyst Dan Ives values Nvidia at $300 a share with Huang and $225 without him.

Nvidia’s new interim CEO, Colette Kress, reports quarterly earnings on November 17. The decision on Huang now sits with directors weighing a founder’s pull against national security questions in Washington.

The post Can Elon Musk Bring Jensen Huang Back as Nvidia CEO? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Over 35% of Bitcoin Supply Faces Potential Quantum Risk, New Data Shows
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
About 7.12 million Bitcoin, or 35.4% of every coin in existence, now has a weak spot. Most owners can fix it in minutes. Satoshi Nakamoto’s coins may never be fixed. Analytics firm Glassnode counted coins whose “public key” already shows on Bitcoin’s public ledger. Think of a public key as a lock anyone can study.

The post Over 35% of Bitcoin Supply Faces Potential Quantum Risk, New Data Shows appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
About 7.12 million Bitcoin, or 35.4% of every coin in existence, now has a weak spot. Most owners can fix it in minutes. Satoshi Nakamoto’s coins may never be fixed.

Analytics firm Glassnode counted coins whose “public key” already shows on Bitcoin’s public ledger. Think of a public key as a lock anyone can study. Today’s computers cannot pick it. A large enough quantum computer, in theory, could, and then move the coins.

Whose Bitcoin is Exposed?

Glassnode says 25.8% of supply is exposed because people reused addresses.

Exchanges hold 11.6% of supply in exposed addresses. Glassnode’s entity data puts Robinhood at 100%, Binance at 85% and Coinbase at about 5%. US government holdings show none. Glassnode says these are not security ratings.

Coinbase holds Bitcoin for most US spot ETFs. One of its analysts has warned of quantum threats, and on October 29 its CEO said work is underway.

“We have begun the work to upgrade our custody to be post-quantum.”

Why Satoshi’s Coins Can’t Be Fixed

For reused addresses, one transaction ends the risk.

“Moving those coins to a fresh address ends this exposure,” Glassnode noted.

About 1 million BTC sits in early addresses linked to Satoshi, according to Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake. They have not moved in over 15 years.

A draft proposal from Casa’s Jameson Lopp would freeze coins that never upgrade, Satoshi’s included. Blockstream CEO Adam Back prefers optional upgrades.

Should Investors Worry Yet?

In March, Google said a quantum machine with under 500,000 qubits could break this kind of encryption in minutes. No such machine exists. Back has said one may be 20 to 40 years away.

At Bitcoin’s current market price, the exposed coins are worth more than $500 billion. An earlier ARK Invest estimate flagged over $480 billion. CoinShares counted only about 10,200 BTC worth targeting for real market impact.

Nasdaq-listed Next Technology Holding approved selling or pledging about 5,833 BTC on October 30, citing quantum computing among other risks.

Lopp’s plan and BIP-360, a separate draft, have no activation date. The quantum threat timeline remains Bitcoin’s open question.

The post Over 35% of Bitcoin Supply Faces Potential Quantum Risk, New Data Shows appeared first on BeInCrypto.

The post XRP Price Faces a Potential 20% Drop: Key Levels to Watch appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
XRP is back at the $1 line, and the next break could be costly. The token traded near $1.03 on November 13 after losing around 15% in a week. 

It briefly slipped below $1 during Friday’s sell-off before recovering, leaving buyers with little room for another setback.

The bigger concern is that XRP’s technical structure continues to weaken. A sustained breakdown could expose another 20% decline, even as oversold signals suggest a possible short-term recovery.

Why XRP Could Fall Another 20%

The most important level now sits near $0.99, the lower boundary of a descending price channel that has contained XRP’s recent decline.

An earlier recovery stalled near $1.55, and subsequent rallies have struggled to regain lost ground. The pattern suggests sellers remain in control.

If XRP loses $0.99 decisively, the next support zones sit around $0.97 and 0.93–0.96. 

Continued selling could eventually push the price toward $0.80, roughly 22% below $1.03.

A brief dip below support would be less significant than repeated daily closes beneath it, particularly if selling volume increases.

The broader cryptocurrency crash adds to the risk. Bitcoin fell below $69,000 on Friday as inflation concerns, fund outflows and liquidations weighed on the market.

Could XRP Price Recover Instead?

XRP’s daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) has fallen into the low 20s, indicating unusually heavy selling pressure. Such conditions can precede a relief rally.

Historical data offers some encouragement. Research covering 17 previous oversold XRP signals found that 70.6% produced positive returns after 90 days. However, the median deepest drawdown during those periods reached 21.8%.

As Bitrue Research cautioned:

“Oversold readings show that selling has been intense, not that it has ended.”

For a recovery, XRP must first clear 1.09–1.11, followed by 1.15–1.16. Reclaiming 1.20–1.25 with stronger buying volume could open the path toward $1.38.

Until then, $0.99 remains the key level separating a potential recovery from a deeper correction.

The post XRP Price Faces a Potential 20% Drop: Key Levels to Watch appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Crypto Exchange Hacks and What You Shouldn't Conclude From Them
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Senra
item.description:
On October 29, in about twenty minutes, $6.3 billion left Binance’s wallets. The largest crypto theft in history, more than four times the Bybit hack of February 2025. The entry point, according to the exchange itself, was an engineer’s computer, infected after a fake job interview. Two days later, Binance announced it had restored 98%

The post Crypto Exchange Hacks and What You Shouldn't Conclude From Them appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
On October 29, in about twenty minutes, $6.3 billion left Binance’s wallets. The largest crypto theft in history, more than four times the Bybit hack of February 2025.

The entry point, according to the exchange itself, was an engineer’s computer, infected after a fake job interview.

Two days later, Binance announced it had restored 98% of the assets with its own funds; the next day, it resumed withdrawals.

Hold on to that last fact. It’s the most important one, and the least talked about.

To a Man with a Hammer, Every Problem Looks Like a Nail

Mt. Gox, 2014. QuadrigaCX, 2019. FTX, 2022. Bybit, 2025. Binance, 2026, to name just the most notorious. Different problems, always the same answer: self-custody, because, after all, not your keys, not your coins.

The premise is technically true. If you don’t hold the private key, you don’t control the asset: you have a claim against whoever does.

The conclusion usually drawn from it isn’t that self-custody is, necessarily, safer.

The Graveyard of the Defeated is Silent, Unless the Defeated is Very Big

When an exchange is attacked, the whole world sees it. There are billions at stake, an official statement, and international coverage.

When an individual loses everything, almost nobody finds out. Even if the loss is on-chain, strictly public, who among the general public follows blockchain investigations?! The general public follows the press.

Many of these victims don’t even file a police report, out of shame or disbelief.

On this side, the investigators’ side, the scene is familiar: the victim shows up with transaction hashes and the hope that someone will “freeze the bitcoins.” 

And, unless the planets align (a victim who reports quickly and well, a qualified public official, funds that end up at an exchange or in freezable tokens), the outcome is dreadful.

Attacks on big exchanges aren’t the most frequent. They’re just the ones everyone sees.

A special Selection from the Self-custody Risk Menu

Handing over the seed. On January 10, 2026, an investor read out his hardware wallet’s seed to a scammer posing as Trezor support. He lost 1,459 BTC and 2.05 million LTC, more than $282 million. The device worked perfectly. Its owner didn’t.

Seed compromise. A photo on your phone, a note in the cloud, an email to yourself. Nobody asked for the words: they simply leaked.

Signature phishing. You sign an off-chain message that authorizes third parties to move your tokens, and they leave whenever the attacker wants. Think of a blank signed check, forgotten in a stranger’s drawer. In January 2026 alone, that came to $6.3 million. 

The irony: the Binance hack also went through signatures. The exchange’s system was tricked into signing 50 authorizations at once, and one was enough to hand the attacker a wallet that lost $2.2 billion in a single transaction. 

Wrench attack. The name comes from the wrench. No cryptography withstands a physical threat against you or your family. In the first half of 2026, CertiK counted 52 of them, totaling $124 million; 33 in France alone. 

Address poisoning. The scammer plants in your history an address almost identical to a legitimate one. On your next transfer, you copy the wrong one. A single case, in January, cost $12.25 million. 

Device failure. On July 29, ColdCard users who had never connected their device to the internet were drained because of a randomness flaw in key generation. More than a thousand bitcoins. I analyzed the case in “Not your keys, not your coins — but do you know how your keys are generated?“.

Notice: in each case, the victim trusted something. The support line, the cloud, the website, their own discretion, the transaction history, the firmware. And, in every case, they trusted their own ability.

Self-custody or Exchange? The False Dilemma

Every form of custody carries risk. Whoever leaves assets on an exchange trusts its governance and solvency. Whoever self-custodies trusts themselves, the device, the software, and whoever knows they own bitcoin. The problem is acknowledging the first and ignoring the second.

There’s no option without trust. There’s conscious trust and ignored trust. And the most expensive risk is the one you don’t see.

Nobody should keep all their wealth under the mattress, nor all of it in a single bank.

With crypto assets, the logic should be the same: part on a solid exchange (or three of them), part in well-done self-custody, part in ETFs — 30%, 40% and 30%, for example. 

The split depends on your knowledge, your profile, and your goals. That responsibility can’t be delegated. Sorry for the bad news, but better now than later.

The Day After Tomorrow

Responsibility reduces risks, but doesn’t eliminate them. So don’t just ask “which option is safest for me?” but also “what would happen to me after an attack?”

In self-custody, there’s no one to call. January’s $282 million started being converted into Monero right away (BTC, BTC, LTC). Freezes happen when the money touches a stablecoin issuer or an exchange. Full recovery is the exception.

On an exchange, there’s a counterparty. Bybit restored its customers’ backing in three days. Bitget covered the $388 million taken in September with its protection fund. 

Binance took on 100% of the loss and has already restored 98%, verifiable in its proof of reserves.

A counterparty, of course, is only worth something if it’s solvent. And it doesn’t always give back exactly what you had.

Mt. Gox creditors waited a decade and got back only about 15% of the bitcoins they “had.” Thanks to the appreciation over that period, though, that fraction was worth many times their entire 2014 balance. 

FTX creditors got cash, not the crypto assets in their balances: about 120% of their value at the collapse, in November 2022, with bitcoin near $16,000. More than they were worth at the time; far less than they’d be worth today. 

Hence the importance, in Brazil, of Central Bank (BCB) Resolutions 519, 520 and 521, of 2025. 

For investors, what matters most isn’t that the exchange answers to the Central Bank, but the requirements it’s subject to: customer assets segregated from the company’s, in separate wallets, with proof of reserves and independent audits, and barred from use in the company’s own operations 

The Bottom Line

Not your keys, not your coins is a maxim about control, not about security.

Whoever pulls all their wealth off exchanges doesn’t stop trusting. They just shift that trust, almost always to themselves, without ever asking whether they deserve it.

Custody isn’t choosing whom not to trust. It’s choosing, consciously, whom to trust, what

The post Crypto Exchange Hacks and What You Shouldn't Conclude From Them appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.dc:creator: Mohammad Shahid
item.description:
The United States has ordered a nationwide halt to flight departures after a major air traffic control communications failure, raising fresh concerns for airline stocks already under pressure on Wall Street. Every US airport was ordered to stop departures on Friday afternoon, November 13, just six minutes before Wall Street closed. The sudden shutdown threatens

The post US Shuts Down All Flights, Stock Market Faces Major Risk appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The United States has ordered a nationwide halt to flight departures after a major air traffic control communications failure, raising fresh concerns for airline stocks already under pressure on Wall Street.

Every US airport was ordered to stop departures on Friday afternoon, November 13, just six minutes before Wall Street closed. The sudden shutdown threatens to disrupt thousands of flights and could leave major airlines facing a costly weekend.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued the order around 3:54 p.m. Eastern, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.”

According to Reuters, aircraft already airborne could continue flying and land, while international arrivals would be handled individually.

What Caused the Nationwide Flight Shutdown?

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that communications problems were affecting regional air traffic control centers responsible for directing aircraft across the country.

The FAA had already halted traffic in Chicago shortly before issuing the nationwide order.

Technicians are investigating the failure. The agency has yet to identify its underlying cause or announce when normal departures will resume.

The disruption follows another major technology failure. A global Microsoft 365 outage, which began Thursday, continued affecting Outlook and Teams on Friday.

However, there is no confirmed connection between Microsoft’s problems and the FAA failure.

Airline Stocks Face Another Major Risk

The shutdown arrived during an already difficult week for aviation stocks.

On Thursday, United Airlines (UAL) fell 6.0%, American Airlines (AAL) dropped 5.6%, and Delta Air Lines (DAL) lost 5.2%. Those declines occurred before Friday’s grounding.

The broader market also finished Friday lower. The Nasdaq lost 0.9%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.4%, according to AP market data.

The FAA announcement came too late to establish a meaningful stock-market reaction during regular trading.

Now, investors face a new uncertainty. Extended flight cancellations could increase operating costs and disrupt airline schedules well beyond Friday.

Monday’s market reopening could become the first major test for airline stocks, particularly if the FAA’s communications problems remain unresolved through the weekend.

The post US Shuts Down All Flights, Stock Market Faces Major Risk appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.content:encoded:
First it was Mukesh Ambani. Now India’s other telecom billionaire, Sunil Mittal, has a condition for Elon Musk: Starlink can come, but the power to switch it off stays in India.

Last month, Musk mocked Ambani as India’s “real boss” for keeping out Starlink, SpaceX’s satellite internet service.

What Did Airtel’s Chairman Say About Starlink?

Sunil Bharti Mittal, chairman of India’s No. 2 carrier Bharti Airtel, told NDTV on November 13 that Musk seems impatient and frustrated. His group backs OneWeb, a Starlink rival also still waiting for approval.

Mittal said Starlink selling in India is “all right.” But control must stay local.

“The kill switch has to be in India. The control has to be in India,” he said.

A kill switch is the power to slow or shut a network down.

Why Does Ukraine Matter Here?

In Ukraine, Starshield, SpaceX’s military version of Starlink, was slowed from Oct. 14 to 24, United24 reported.

Musk said it was decided by the US President, Donald Trump.

Why is Starlink’s Design a Problem for India?

Starlink satellites pass data to each other by laser, so traffic can skip Indian ground stations. OneWeb has no such links, Mittal said. According to Tech Insider, India’s security rules clash with that laser design.

Mukesh Ambani’s Jio Platforms listed Oct. 28 at ₹1,119 ($11.68) a share in India’s largest IPO. It traded near ₹1,400 on Nov. 13.

Starlink’s main overlap with Jio is home broadband, where Jio holds 42.6% of fixed lines. Jio also holds 77.5% of 5G home wireless. Until Starlink is cleared, it cannot sell a single dish against either.

Musk accused Ambani of blocking him, BeInCrypto reported. India denies bias and says Starlink filed security papers last.

What’s in it for Airtel?

In October, Mittal said he would be happy to win approval a few days before Musk. He also doubts demand. Indians get 5G almost anywhere for about $3 a month, he said, so why pay ten times more for satellite?

India’s Cabinet must still set the spectrum fee. The Home Ministry must clear each operator. Until then, nobody sells.

The post After Mukesh Ambani, India’s Other Telecom Billionaire Targets Elon Musk appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.content:encoded:
Twenty One Capital reported a $1.087 billion third-quarter profit on Friday. The money came from Bitcoin (BTC) rising in value, and about 60% of it has already disappeared.

Bitcoin has fallen since the quarter closed on Sept. 30. The Texas firm’s coins are now worth about $700 million less than it paid.

Where Did Twenty One Capital’s $1 Billion Profit Come From?

US accounting rules require companies to book changes in the value of crypto they hold as profit or loss. No coins need to be sold.

At the end of September, each Bitcoin was worth about $83,700, the company’s quarterly filing shows. That price lifted its 43,514 coins by $1.093 billion.

Meanwhile, the business itself reported no revenue. It posted a $4.8 million operating loss for the quarter.

Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Rapha Zagury, who took over after Jack Mallers stepped down in July, drew the same line.

“But gains from an asset we own are not the same as earnings from businesses we operate,” Rapha Zagury, CEO of Twenty One Capital, in his shareholder letter.

How Much of the $1 Billion Is Left?

On Nov. 13, the coins were worth about $2.99 billion, according to BitcoinTreasuries. That is about $653 million below their quarter-end value, roughly 60% of the profit.

The company paid about $3.69 billion for the coins, its filing shows. As a result, the holdings now sit roughly $700 million below cost.

The same rule worked in reverse earlier this year. Bitcoin’s decline produced a $1.27 billion net loss in the first half of 2026.

Even after the third-quarter gain, the company remains $186.5 million in the red for the year.

Investors did not cheer. XXI shares traded at $4.97 at midday Friday, down 0.6%.

Zagury said buybacks deserve serious consideration if the stock trades below its asset value. However, he conceded the company cannot call Bitcoin’s next move.

“…we have no idea where Bitcoin price is going to be a year from now,” Rapha Zagury, on the earnings call.

Twenty One Capital ranks among the largest corporate Bitcoin holders, so its earnings now rise and fall with the coin. If Bitcoin ends December below $83,700, the same rule will book a fourth-quarter loss on its holdings.

item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin sank to about $68,000 on Friday. That is its lowest price since August. US stocks tied to the coin went down with it.

The companies that mine new Bitcoin took the worst hit. Hut 8 dropped 6%. Riot Platforms and MARA Holdings each lost 3.9%. Coinbase, the largest US crypto exchange, slipped just 0.5%.

Why is Bitcoin Falling?

It started with prices at the shops. US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Tuesday.

Traders now bet the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December. Higher rates make risky bets like Bitcoin less attractive.

“Given the higher-than-desired inflation, it is even more likely now that the Fed will raise rates in December,” Chris Zaccarelli of Northlight Asset Management said.

Friday brought no relief. Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, below forecasts. But the yearly rate climbed to 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years. Wall Street’s early gains vanished within 30 minutes. The S&P 500 slid 0.55% and the Nasdaq 0.64%.

Why Do Miners Fall Harder?

Miners earn in Bitcoin. When the coin drops, so does their income. Power bills and debts do not.

MARA shows the squeeze. Its mining made $30.1 million after direct costs last quarter, against $43.9 million in overheads. About 54% of its Bitcoin is pledged against loans.

Not everyone sees doom. Miners are renting their power sites to artificial intelligence firms. Last week, Riot and Hut 8 each jumped 12% on those hopes while bitcoin stood still.

What Comes Next?

Strategy, the biggest corporate bitcoin holder, faces its own deadline. Index provider MSCI will drop it from its benchmarks after November 30.

JPMorgan analysts estimated that could force about $2.8 billion in selling. Strategy says index funds hold about 13 million shares, less than a day’s trading.

The bigger test is the Fed’s December meeting.

item.content:encoded:
On December 14–20, 2026, Synopsis will host TOP Crypto Voices, it’s seventh international online summit. The seven-day programme is set to bring together more than 50 crypto industry leaders for presentations, interviews and panel discussions on the next stage of Web3 development. The summit will be streamed on the Synopsis YouTube channel.

Since 2021, Synopsis has brought together founders, executives and investors from leading companies across the crypto industry. Across six editions, 150 projects have been represented at the summit, from Binance, Coinbase and Bitget to Animoca Brands, Ava Labs, Offchain Labs and Bitwise. Its speakers build Web3 infrastructure, manage capital and set the strategic direction of the market’s largest players.

In 2026, the crypto industry’s integration into the global financial system gained fresh momentum. Morgan Stanley launched its own crypto exchange-traded products, while BlackRock expanded its offering with an ETH product featuring staking.

CME Group moved crypto futures and options to 24/7 trading. Fidelity introduced the FIDD stablecoin, and PayPal expanded access to PYUSD to 70 markets. The SEC, with input from the CFTC, issued guidance on the application of US law to crypto assets. What do these developments mean for the crypto market — and which will shape the agenda for 2027?

Synopsis TOP Crypto Voices brings this conversation to the decision-makers: protocol founders, exchange executives, investors and Web3 infrastructure builders. Discussions will focus on where capital is flowing, which technologies are seeing real-world adoption and what will shape competition in the crypto market in 2027.

The Synopsis agenda spans the key areas driving growth and competition across the crypto industry: Bitcoin and ETFs, investment, stablecoins and global payments, institutional tokenisation and RWA, AI agents, DeFi, trading and exchange infrastructure. Particular attention will be given to regulation, investment strategies, mining, ZK technologies and cross-chain protocols.

Partners and Residents: TRON, Arbitrum, Binance, Bitget, Ava Labs, Wormhole, Algorand, Monad, Mysten Labs, LI.FI, Paxos Labs, Bitget Wallet, Biconomy.com, Stable, Symbiotic, Animoca Brands, Bitwise, Offchain Labs, Injective, THETA, Sei Labs, The Graph, Pyth Network, Sonic, Polygon, Plume, Ledger, KuCoin, dYdX, Vaulta, 21Shares, PancakeSwap, Ryze Labs, BIT Mining (NYSE: BTCM), Bitfury and many others

  • Organiser: Synopsis Web3 Summit
  • Dates: December 14–20, 2026
  • Venue: youtube.com/@Synopsis_ 

A Front-Row Seat from Anywhere in the World

Watch presentations, interviews and panel discussions with industry leaders from wherever you are. Seven days to compare the perspectives of investors, exchanges and protocol developers — and see where their outlooks on the market’s future converge and where they differ.

Join Synopsis Edition 7: “TOP Crypto Voices”

Save the dates, subscribe to the Synopsis YouTube channel and turn on notifications.Follow Synopsis on X for the latest updates and key announcements.
